anchors: A pattern must also MISS every other refusal the code can raise.
so a pattern for the inner rule also passes when the wrapper fires
decision: A pytest.raises match= pattern must match its own refusal and no other the code can raise: check it with re.search against every raise message in the module and the layers it calls, anchor an inner rule's pattern against a wrapper that interpolates it, and give a test-raised sentinel a whole-matched sentence.

evidence.text: A scan of one library's suite flagged 42 single-token patterns; recording every refusal message the suite raised (551) showed several patterns, and a new alternation pattern, matching unrelated refusals of the same package. RED arms (opus, haiku) on the pre-edit text both listed the missing neighbour check as a skill gap; GREEN arms on both tiers rejected the loose patterns quoting the new sentence.

reopen_if: pytest changes match= from re.search to a full match, or a shipped tool checks every pattern against the code's refusal set automatically in the gate.
why: match= is re.search, so a word several refusals share passes whichever fires and the test stays green when the code refuses for the wrong reason. The earlier text only said to match the validator's phrase and allowed any substring every arm shares.

anchors: A budget the code spends waiting on a stand-in that must ANSWER is roomy
decision: A budget the code spends waiting on a stand-in that must answer is roomy; only a test expecting expiry keeps a tight one; a pacing TCP stand-in turns Nagle off and the test asserts the outcome class and reported == on-disk bytes, never bytes-within-budget.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for Nagle/NODELAY. GREEN opus and haiku: both fixed the trickle test (Nagle off, outcome plus on-disk bytes) and the 1 s vote budget, and left the expiring-budget control alone, quoting the bullet.

reopen_if: A suite following this still flakes on stand-in timing, or a roomy budget hides a real hang.
why: A 1 s budget let one stall on a loaded host flip an unrelated vote about once in three full runs; with Nagle on, macOS delivered 6 of 18 trickled bytes where Linux and Windows delivered all, costing two red CI rounds.

anchors: with every inherited `GIT_*` variable removed first
RED one arm per sink: in a scratch copy
assert an outcome only the timed wake produces
decision: Three defeater entries: a fresh-home commit test sets GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* in a child env stripped of inherited GIT_* with XDG_CONFIG_HOME under the temp dir; a refused-before-side-effect test asserts every sink, RED one arm per sink; a timed-wake test uses a case only the timeout can wake, asserts an outcome only the timed wake produces, and bounds the untimed-wait arm.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for _AUTHOR_/_COMMITTER_, untimed, every sink. GREEN opus and haiku found each seeded defect; gaps closed (zero-completed outcome, bounded arm, GIT_* strip, untouched defined) and a haiku re-run on the final text applied all three.

reopen_if: A test written to one of these entries still passes against the defect it names.
why: Each passed locally and failed in CI or survived a mutation: a commit test red only on a runner with no identity, a zero-timeout test green while every proxy was banned, an untimed-wait mutant surviving a many-short-items test.

anchors: Bind it and keep it referenced past the count
decision: A leak check after a refused call binds the pytest.raises result and keeps it referenced past the count.

evidence.text: Probe: a function opening a file and raising without close; the unbound pytest.raises form passed, the bound form failed on the leak.

reopen_if: The suite counts resources only with gc and refcount effects excluded some other way.
why: Releasing the exception frees the frames holding the leaked object, refcounting closes it, and the count returns to baseline on leaking code.

anchors: an autouse fixture that isolates the suite by setting the OVERRIDE wins over every test that sets the plain knob itself
is found by every test that counts that search's results
decision: An autouse isolation fixture for an override-plus-fallback lookup points every platform's fallback knob under the temp dir and deletes the override with setenv then delenv; a file it plants to stop an upward search is expected by, or bypassed by name in, every test that counts that search's results.

evidence.text: Probe: a lookup LIB_X_ROOT-or-APPDATA with a test setting APPDATA failed under an override-setting autouse fixture and passed under a fallback-setting one that removed the override with setenv then delenv.

reopen_if: The lookup under test gives the plain knob precedence over the override.
why: A fixture-set override wins over every test that sets the plain knob itself, so those tests fail or pass vacuously, often on one platform only; a planted sentinel is included in every count of that search.

anchors: refuses every input the real tool refuses, with the same usage error and exit
decision: A hand-written fake of a CLI the code shells out to refuses every input the real tool refuses, with the same usage error and exit code; for a tool you own, the fake calls the tool's own validator or one test runs the real tool on a scratch tree.

evidence.text: Contribution report: a fake of an owned CLI accepted an argument value the real tool rejects, all 64 tests passed, and the first real dry run exposed it. RED quote-back on opus and haiku against the pre-edit text answered NONE for argument values and exit codes.

reopen_if: A contract test that runs every fake against its real tool becomes part of the standard harness, making a per-fake rule redundant.
why: A fake more lenient than the tool keeps the suite green on calls production fails with; the existing seam-shape rule covered a callable's keywords and return shape, not a CLI's argument values or exit codes.

anchors: honours the stop condition the real one has
decision: A fake standing in for a waiter, poller or child process honours the stop condition the real one has (the --timeout or deadline the code passes it) and answers with the real tool's timed-out result once that limit is spent.

evidence.text: Contribution report: in a 13-arm mutation battery one arm read as a hang until the fake waiter modelled the real tool's timeout. RED quote-back on opus and haiku against the pre-edit text answered NONE.

reopen_if: Mutation tooling learns to classify an arm that hangs to its timeout as killed, so a hang reads the same as a failing assertion.
why: A fake that ignores the limit turns the mutant removing the code's own stop into a hang until the outer timeout, which reads as neither killed nor survived.

anchors: skips every name matching `dummy-variable-rgx`, whose default matches any name starting with `_`
decision: A module-level def or class name defined twice keeps only the last definition for every caller; ruff F811 is not relied on for it, and the shape is closed by an ast repo test over tree.body that skips module-level if/try blocks and typing.overload stubs and fails on zero files examined.

evidence.text: ruff 0.15.0, 0.16.0 and 0.17.5 with --select F811: a plain redefinition of `helper` is reported, the same file with `_helper` is not, and two real duplicate pairs of underscore helpers were not reported until dummy-variable-rgx was narrowed to ^_$. A module-level use between the defs suppresses the report even for a plain name.

reopen_if: ruff (or the project's linter) reports a redefinition of an underscore-prefixed top-level def under its default configuration.
why: The earlier helper's tests run the later helper silently. F811 skips every name matching dummy-variable-rgx (by default any name starting with an underscore, which is what test helpers use) and a redefinition whose name is used at module level in between, so no lint gate sees the case that happens.

anchors: Never divide by an arm that did no MEASURABLE work.
decision: A growth-ratio check never divides by an arm that did no measurable work: a constant-work negative case keeps its input, the check returns both arm times, lets a large arm under a floor pass the linearity check without a ratio, and guards the super-linear assertion with small > 0.

evidence.text: A macOS CI cell read process_time 0.0 for the small arm of r'^\s+x' on 'a' * N and raised ZeroDivisionError; on Linux the same arms read 0.83 us and 0.57 us. The shipped test fix returns both times and counts a large arm under 5 ms as linear.

reopen_if: Every negative case a growth-ratio check uses is required to drive the costly path, so no arm can finish below the clock's step.
why: A negative case whose input never enters the costly path finishes below the clock's step in both arms, so the ratio divides by zero or compares two sub-microsecond readings.

anchors: `os.times().user` reads the same time in whole clock ticks
decision: On POSIX a growth-ratio check reads user CPU time from resource.getrusage (RUSAGE_THREAD, else RUSAGE_SELF), not os.times().user, and measures the step of whatever clock it picks.

evidence.text: On Linux with Python 3.14, reading each clock in a loop until it changed: os.times().user stepped 0.01 s (SC_CLK_TCK 100), resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_utime about 3 us, time.process_time about 0.35 us.

reopen_if: os.times().user gains sub-tick resolution on Linux, or the check's arms are all far longer than a clock tick.
why: os.times().user reads user time in whole clock ticks (10 ms on Linux), so a short arm reads 0.0 or one tick; getrusage steps in microseconds.

anchors: Both arms must do MEASURABLE work.
Then keep a backstop for an arm that is still too fast
decision: A growth-ratio check first gives a constant-work negative case an input that drives the costly path, sized so the small arm stays far above the clock's step; the floor (both arm times returned, a large arm under a floor passing without a ratio, small > 0 guarding the super-linear assertion) is only the backstop for an arm still too fast.

evidence.text: On Linux, r'^\s+x' over ' ' * N took 0.06 ms at 50,000, 0.42 ms at 400,000 and 4.3 ms at 4,000,000 user time per pass, while 'a' * N read 0.0 in both arms; a macOS CI cell raised ZeroDivisionError on the 'a' * N case. Two quote-back probes (opus, haiku) on the final text both answered 'first change the input, the floor is the backstop'.

reopen_if: A negative case is found whose costly path cannot be driven by any input, so the floor is the only defence.
why: Read as two equal options, the floor let a check keep an input that never reaches the costly path, so the check still asserted nothing about growth; the input fix is what makes the arms measure the code.

anchors: `resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_utime`, which counts every thread of the process
fall back to `time.perf_counter()` (accepting
read `ru_utime + ru_stime`
decision: A growth-ratio check reads user CPU time from getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_utime on POSIX (macOS included), with other threads idle; on Windows, where every CPU-time clock steps 15.625 ms, it makes each arm hundreds of milliseconds long and falls back to perf_counter only where it cannot; a test whose cost IS page faulting reads ru_utime + ru_stime; every clock choice is checked against a busy-loop arm of known length.

evidence.text: Linux 7.0, Python 3.14, busy-loop arms: RUSAGE_SELF read a 0.1 ms arm as 0.10-0.11 ms, RUSAGE_THREAD as 0.0 or about 1 ms, os.times().user as 0.0 (10 ms ticks). Windows 11 26200, Python 3.14.6 (the Windows dev box): os.times().user, process_time and thread_time all stepped 0.015625 s, a 2 ms arm read 0.0 in 18 of 20 runs. Faulting in 256 MiB of fresh mmap pages: 0.086 s system, 0.008 s user.

reopen_if: Windows gains a sub-millisecond process CPU clock in Python, or RUSAGE_THREAD stops quantising on Linux.
why: RUSAGE_THREAD and os.times().user misread short arms on Linux, and no Windows CPU-time clock resolves an arm of a few milliseconds; user time leaves fault handling out, so a fault-cost test needs kernel time too.

anchors: Under pytest-xdist it is worse, not harmless
decision: A conftest COVERAGE_FILE does not redirect a serial pytest-cov run, and under pytest-xdist it sends the workers' data elsewhere so the report reads No data to report; set the variable in the environment that starts pytest.

evidence.text: Probed here (covprobe): serial run wrote .coverage; pytest -n 2 wrote redir/.cov-conftest.* and reported No data to report.

reopen_if: pytest-cov starts resolving the data file in the workers from the controller's setting.
why: The old text called the conftest setting merely ineffective; under xdist it silently zeroes coverage while every test passes.

anchors: **A browser test that only COUNTS or FINDS an overlay never looks at it.**
**Async UI state needs a delay probe per ENTRY PATH.**
decision: Browser tests assert what an overlay looks like (background, size, contrast, clipping) per theme, and async UI state gets a delay probe per entry path.

evidence.text: 2026-11-19 (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: UI frameworks start rendering overlays identically in harness and browser.
why: Counting tests passed transparent full-height dialogs, and green suites with instant fakes missed async ordering defects every probe round found.

anchors: Make each worker pause briefly and at random after every write that took the lock
decision: A race test's stress workers pause briefly and at random after each write that took the lock; the main loop ends on an operation count and the workers stop on a stop file.

evidence.text: Pinned to one cpu beside three busy loops, the unpaced tests failed 4 of 4 in 2 of 2 runs, the paced ones passed 3 of 3, and all four still failed on the pre-fix code. RED probes on opus and haiku answered NONE for the workers.

reopen_if: The locks such tests exercise become fair (FIFO) everywhere the pattern is used, so an immediate retake no longer starves a waiter.
why: A worker that retakes the lock at once leaves a polling waiter no gap, so on a slow runner the test reports lock fairness and runner speed instead of its property; a wall-clock window makes the count depend on runner speed.

anchors: read each WORKER's stderr before reasoning from the assertion
decision: When a multi-process race test fails on one CI cell, read each worker's stderr first; the test sends each worker's stderr to its own file and puts it in the assertion message.

evidence.text: A Windows-only failure read updated=306, ended=deadline until the updater's traceback named an unretried open() refused with Errno 13. RED probes on opus and haiku answered NONE for reading worker stderr first.

reopen_if: The test runner itself collects and prints every child process's stderr on failure.
why: The assertion shows only the symptom (a short count, a deadline reached); the crashed worker's traceback names the failing call.
